text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker. Mr. Speaker, I'm sure you will agree, and I hope others across the chamber will also, that we need to recognize and to celebrate achievements. And I say this because across the country, knife crime offenses is going down. And of course, more needs to be done and more should be done. But this week's figures have shown that London has had its safest year ever under the London Mayor Sadiq Khan. And in fact, homicide rate in London is the lowest ever since records began. Now, Mr. Speaker, Reform and the Conservatives repeatedly talk down our capital city. So will the Prime Minister join me in saying they are wrong and will he applaud these achievements?

What I would say is David, this is a very experienced member and I know he'll pursue this through the many avenues and I know there is a debate later in which he may wish to catch the chair's eye in order to raise these issues. These are very serious issues that he's raised and this will be taken seriously and I'm sure that the front bench has heard it as well. I will leave it at that. Point of order.
